Start exactly from the first frame and continue the same continuous take without any cut; the camera never changes position, height or angle; there is no cutaway, no insert, no second angle, no close-up. The wiry young man in the red suspenders and faded blue serape stands over the saloon card table under a single hard shaft of noon light, chips and cards flying from his hands. The chips land and skitter across the table and onto the plank floor; he throws both arms up in a whoop of triumph, head back, cards still fanned in one fist. Then a black-sleeved arm reaches in from the right edge with a long wooden dealer's rake and drags every chip off the table in one slow sweep, out of frame to the right. His grin collapses as he watches them go; he sinks down onto the wooden chair, lays his cheek on the bare table in the shaft of light, one hand still holding a single card, and lies still while the dust settles in the light.
